Subject: Baseline math for IO charges & how rounding affects committed discount

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the latency profile. Procurement and finance are now digging into the numbers for our internal ratecard comparison. We have two quick, technical questions that would change our model:

1) How do you allocate input vs output tokens for streamed responses when a tool call (e.g., a function that returns a short JSON blob) is included? Is the tool-return counted as output or as system/tool tokens?

2) When you bill per 1k tokens, do you round up per call, per minute of usage, or on aggregate per invoice line? For example, if a single API call has 14.2 output tokens and 25.7 input tokens, does that become 15/26 (rounded per call) or do you sum across the day and round at the invoice line? This matters for our unit economics at scale.

I've attached a tiny sample of our average calls. Can you provide the precise behavior and an example calculation that includes your rounding policy plus any minimums that might affect committed discount tiers?

Appreciate the clarity — finance needs an answer to finalize the supplier scorecard.

Best,

Thanks for the ping — dug into the billing docs and talked to metering. Summary below (draft for external):

- Allocation: We attribute characters/tokens as follows: prompt/input tokens = everything the customer sends (user + system + developer messages when supplied on the request); output tokens = model-generated tokens plus explicit tool return payloads (the tool output is billed as output). However, we additionally report a separate line item called "tool/system tokens" in the console for visibility (customers can see the breakdown), but for the ratecard and invoice the chargeable breakdown is Input vs Output only.

- Rounding granularity: Billing rounds up to the nearest whole token at the invoice aggregation level for each invoice line (not per-call). That means we sum raw fractional token counts across the invoice period and then round up once before applying the 1k-token price banding.

- Streaming: Streaming does not change allocation — partial chunks are accumulated server-side into the same invoice aggregation pool.

- Minimums and discount bands: There is no per-call minimum. Discount tiers are evaluated on the rounded invoice-line totals (so their effective tier is based on rounded aggregated counts).

Examples (useful to send to Acme):
  • Single-call example (explain for clarity only): 14.2 output + 25.7 input -> charged as 14.2 output and 25.7 input in telemetry, but not rounded per call.
  • Daily aggregation example: If across one day they have three calls with output tokens 14.2, 14.2, 7.6 (total 36.0), the invoice-line will round up from 36.0 -> 36 tokens (no change). If total were 36.2 -> round up to 37 tokens for billing.

Caveat: In our hosted pricing engine we price per 1k tokens with per-line (input/output) price. The billing system applies rounding after summing. For certain promotional credits or legacy negotiated SOWs we sometimes apply manual adjustments — those are handled outside the automated rounding flow and reflected as a credit line on the invoice.

I'll draft a customer-facing reply with a concise worked example.

- Karthik

Hi Jordan — thanks for the sample and question. Short answer plus two worked examples below. If you want, we can schedule a 20‑minute call with billing to walk through your real volume profile.

Short answers:
- Tool-return payloads (the JSON blob returned by a function/tool) are counted as output tokens for billing. We also show them separately as "tool/system" in the Console for visibility, but invoice charges are split Input vs Output only.
- We aggregate raw token floats across the invoice period and round up once per invoice line before applying the per-1k rate. We do not round per API call.

Worked examples using your sample (attached file):
Example A — single representative call (for visibility):
  • Input: 25.7 tokens (user prompt + system snippets)
  • Output: 14.2 tokens (LLM text) + 9.1 tokens (tool-return JSON) -> total output telemetry 23.3 tokens
  • What you see in Console: Input = 25.7, Output = 23.3, Tool/System = 9.1 (tool separated for visibility)
  • Billing behavior: we do NOT round this single call in isolation on the invoice. These fractional values accumulate across the billing period.

Example B — invoice-level effect (7 days aggregated simplified):
  • Day totals (sample): Day1 Input 12,345.4 / Output 7,821.6  Day2 Input 11,900.3 / Output 8,176.1  Day3 Input 13,110.2 / Output 7,990.8  (sum Input 37,355.9 / Output 23,988.5)
  • Rounding step (per-line): Input -> round up 37,356 tokens charged; Output -> round up 23,989 tokens charged
  • Pricing step: We apply the per-1k-tiered price to those rounded totals when calculating spend for discount band evaluation.

Discount/commit notes:
- Discount tiers are evaluated against the charged (rounded) totals on the invoice. If you expect borderline behavior (e.g., within ~0.5% of a threshold) we recommend adding a small buffer in the SOW or negotiating a fixed committed token quantity in the contract.
- For negotiated SOWs we can also include a carve-out clause that specifies how rounding is handled for discount thresholds (e.g., floor vs. round). Those adjustments are manual and shown as credit lines — please flag if you prefer that route.

Attachments: ratecard_US_v3.pdf (current list price)

Best,

Monica, Logan — this is exactly what finance needed, thank you. A couple very small follow ups:

1) In the sample day totals you gave, the tool tokens are included inside the Output bucket for billing. Can you confirm the invoice line item wording we should expect? Will the invoice show two lines (Input, Output) and we should expect Output to include tool/system tokens?

2) If we negotiate a committed volume (e.g., 1.2B charged tokens/month), will Redwood ever round down for the purposes of hitting that committed band (e.g., if we invoice-round to 1,199,999.4 -> 1,199,999) or is it always round up? We just want to lock expectations.

If you can confirm those two points in writing we can finalize the supplier scorecard and move the procurement team to the SOW review.
